mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 2.0% indicates an accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate decline below 1.50% signals aggressive monetary easing that boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS falls below 1.50%, SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a robust labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 100k and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: In periods where PAYEMS rises >100k and UNRATE falls >0.2pp, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market recovery (HOUST above 1300 thousand units) and strong consumer spending (RSAFS above 500,000 million dollars), the S&P 500 tends to rise over the next 20 days due to positive economic momentum.
regime_hint: strong housing and consumer spending regime
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST > 1300 and RSAFS > 500000, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in industrial production (INDPRO above 108.0) indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is above 108.0, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI index above 0.2% signals rising inflation that pressures the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 0.2%, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE below 3.5%), the labor market is tight and supports strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 3.5, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a 'higher for longer' monetary policy that is supportive of equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.1pp and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS decreases >0.1pp and CPIAUCSL increases >0.2%, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.
